fractions_decimals.questionBridge: Simon slides the ledger toward you. Break the whole into parts. Every tenth counts.

ratios_proportions.settingLine: Giza, foot of the pyramid, 600 BC
ratios_proportions.questionBridge: Thales measures the shadow against his staff. If one thing scales, so does the other.

order_of_operations.questionBridge: Ada taps the punch cards. Do the steps in the right order. The machine forgives nothing.

basic_equations.questionBridge: Diophantus scratches a riddle into the wax. A number is hiding. Undo each step until you find it.

linear_equations.questionBridge: William stares at the balance. One unknown. Find what makes both sides equal.

functions_basics.questionBridge: Euler scrawls f(x). Feed it a number and watch what comes out.

right_triangle_geometry.questionBridge: Pythagoras watches the knotted rope snap taut. Two sides quietly fix the third. Find the pact between them.

trigonometry_basics.questionBridge: Hipparchus lowers his instrument. Angles and sides are bound together. Use one to find the other.

linear_inequalities.settingLine: USAF logistics office, the Berlin Airlift, 1948
linear_inequalities.questionBridge: George maps the constraints. The answer is not one number. It is a region. Find where every limit holds at once.

systems_of_linear_equations.questionBridge: Liu Hui lays the counting rods in rows. Two unknowns, two conditions. Make them agree at once.

exponent_rules.questionBridge: Archimedes climbs his tower of tens. Don't multiply the giants. Add the floors they stand on.

polynomials.questionBridge: Niccolò sketches the cannonball's path in the margin. Many terms, one curve. Combine what matches, layer by layer.

factoring_polynomials.questionBridge: Pierre hunts the hidden square inside the number. Every product is a disguise. Find what multiplied to build it.

radical_expressions.questionBridge: Hippasus lowers his voice. Some numbers hide under the root sign. Handle them exactly.

quadratic_equations.questionBridge: Galileo marks where the ball lands. The rise and the fall cross the same height twice. Find both.

descriptive_statistics.questionBridge: Florence sets down her pen. What does the data actually say?

basic_probability.questionBridge: Blaise counts every path the dice could take. Before you wager, map every future, then take your share of it.
basic_probability.diceFrame: Pascal shakes the dice in his cupped hands and slams them onto the table.
basic_probability.spinnerFrame: Pascal flicks the pointer into a blur and dares you to call where it stops.

exponential_functions.questionBridge: Max watches the case count double again. Growth that feeds on itself outruns you fast. Recognize the curve before it explodes.

logarithmic_functions.questionBridge: John slides his great table across the desk. To undo a power, ask what exponent got you there.

sequences_series.questionBridge: Carl reaches for his slate. There is a pattern in the terms. Find it before you count.

lines_angles.questionBridge: Eratosthenes measures the obelisk's short shadow. One angle, carried across parallel lines, tells you the rest.

triangles_congruence.questionBridge: Villard lays the two trusses side by side. Match enough sides and angles and the shapes cannot help but agree.

circles_geometry.settingLine: Jiankang, the Liu Song court, China, 5th century AD
circles_geometry.questionBridge: Zu doubles the polygon's sides again. Every point on the rim stays the same distance from the center. Build from that promise.

area_volume.settingLine: Egypt, copying the Rhind Papyrus, 1550 BC
area_volume.questionBridge: Ahmes counts the invisible squares across the surface, then stacks the layers. The space must answer in numbers.

geometric_transformations.questionBridge: Maurits studies the tiles. Slide it, flip it, turn it, and ask what stays the same.

rational_expressions.settingLine: Rome, commissioner of the aqueducts, 97 AD
rational_expressions.questionBridge: Sextus reduces every pipe to a common measure. Treat the top and bottom with equal rigor, or the ledger lies.

complex_numbers.questionBridge: Rafael refuses to discard the impossible number. Follow the rules anyway. They still hold.

vectors.questionBridge: Josiah splits the arrow into its parts. Magnitude alone is a rumor. Direction is what makes it true.

matrices.questionBridge: Arthur arranges the numbers into a grid. The grid itself obeys algebra. Work it row by column.

conic_sections.questionBridge: Johannes checks the data once more. Slice the cone. The curve tells you which cut was made.

probability_distributions.questionBridge: Abraham tallies a thousand trials. Chance has a shape. Read the whole distribution.

applications_of_derivatives.questionBridge: Katherine checks the trajectory by hand. Find where the rate goes to zero. That is the turning point that matters.

integrals.questionBridge: Johannes slices the barrel into disks thinner than hairs. Add up the small pieces. The total is exact.

applications_of_integrals.settingLine: Torquay, England, the naval testing tank, 1870
applications_of_integrals.questionBridge: William slices the hull into cross-sections. Accumulate the small pieces, because the whole must hold.

inferential_statistics.questionBridge: Richard reads the serial number off the gearbox. One sample proves nothing alone. Test what the evidence can bear.

number_properties.questionBridge: Srinivasa sees the pattern before anyone else. This number has a personality. Learn it before it surprises you.

measurement_units.questionBridge: Arthur traces the fault line by line. Convert precisely and carry the units through, or the whole calculation lies.

algebraic_manipulation.questionBridge: Muhammad calls it al-jabr, the restoring. Rearrange the symbols. Keep both sides in balance.

representation_translation.questionBridge: René sees the same truth in a graph, a table, an equation. Translate between them.

act_strategy.questionBridge: Enrico drops a handful of torn paper into the wind. Before you compute anything precisely, decide what the answer must roughly be.

coordinate_geometry.questionBridge: Descartes watches a fly on the ceiling. Two numbers are enough to name any point.

absolute_value.questionBridge: Argand draws the number line. Distance from zero: direction doesn't matter here.

integer_operations.questionBridge: Brahmagupta argues that debts are real numbers. Work with what you have.

polynomial_operations.questionBridge: Cardano combines the terms carefully. Like with like. Simplify until it's clean.

percent_ratio.questionBridge: Pacioli checks the ledger. Out of every hundred: what portion is this?

data_interpretation.questionBridge: Snow marks each case on the map. The data is telling a story. Read it.

combinatorics.questionBridge: Pascal writes to Fermat. How many ways can this happen? Count them all.

derivatives.questionBridge: Isaac watches the apple fall. Don't average the whole flight, freeze one instant. That's the rate you want.
